questions.question: Abhi rows upstream a distance of 28 km in 4 h and rows downstream a distance of 50 km in 2 h to row a distance of 44.8 km in still water, he will take∶
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Upstream Speed = 28 ÷ 4 = 7 kmph

Downstream Speed = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 kmph

Speed of boat in still water = (Upstream + Downstream) ÷ 2 = (7 + 25) ÷ 2 = 16 kmph

Required time = 44.8 ÷ 16 = 2.8 h

**∴ The correct answer is 2.8 h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Upstream distance = 28 km in 4 h, Downstream distance = 50 km in 2 h.

Formula Used: Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Speed in Still Water (v) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b3a9cb72d8df6bbe9dd0b6ee6058b2d28ec0872c228e3dfce9f5bfaf639a4fa.png] 

⇒ Upstream speed (u) = 28 ÷ 4 = 7 kmph

⇒ Downstream speed (d) = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 kmph

⇒ Speed of boat in still water (v) = (d + u) ÷ 2

⇒ v = (25 + 7) ÷ 2 = 32 ÷ 2 = 16 kmph

⇒ Time taken to cover 44.8 km in still water = Distance ÷ v

⇒ Time = 44.8 ÷ 16 = 2.8 h

**∴ The correct answer is 2.8 h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water (v)

The speed of the boat when the water is stationary. v = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream (s)

The rate at which the river water flows. s = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Downstream and Upstream Speed

Downstream Speed = v + s; Upstream Speed = v − s.</p

questions.question: A boat can go 5 km upstream and 7.5 km downstream in 45 minutes. It can also go 5 km downstream and 2.5 km upstream in 25 minutes. How much time (in minutes) will it take to go 6 km upstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Scale the second case by 2: 5 km Upstream + 10 km Downstream = 50 minutes.

Compare with the first case: 5 km Upstream + 7.5 km Downstream = 45 minutes.

The difference of 2.5 km Downstream takes 5 minutes (50 − 45), so 5 km Downstream takes 10 minutes.

From the scaled second case, 5 km Upstream takes 50 − 10 = 40 minutes, which means 1 km Upstream takes 8 minutes? No, let's re-evaluate from the original second case.

In Case 2: 2.5 km Upstream + (5 km Downstream = 10 min) = 25 minutes → 2.5 km Upstream takes 15 minutes.

Rate Upstream = 15 ÷ 2.5 = 6 minutes per km. For 6 km Upstream = 6 × 6 = 36 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: 5 km Upstream + 7.5 km Downstream = 45 minutes

Case 2: 2.5 km Upstream + 5 km Downstream = 25 minutes

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef6be56925d07a743336ac4dc15d7d9bfc49936e11f69c72ef4f12c5e1a6086e.png] 

Let the time taken to travel 1 km upstream be 'u' and 1 km downstream be 'd'.

⇒ 5u + 7.5d = 45 — (i)

⇒ 2.5u + 5d = 25 — (ii)

Multiply equation (ii) by 1.5 to match 'd' coefficients:

⇒ 3.75u + 7.5d = 37.5 — (iii)

Subtract equation (iii) from equation (i):

⇒ (5u − 3.75u) + (7.5d − 7.5d) = 45 − 37.5

⇒ 1.25u = 7.5

⇒ u = 7.5 ÷ 1.25

⇒ u = 6 minutes/km

This 'u' is the time required to travel 1 km upstream.

⇒ Time for 6 km upstream = 6 × u

⇒ Time = 6 × 6 = 36 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 36 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Upstream and Downstream Speed

If boat speed is B and stream speed is S, then Downstream Speed (D) = B + S and Upstream Speed (U) = B − S.

Boat and Stream Speed from U and D

Boat speed in still water (B) = (D + U) ÷ 2 and Stream speed (S) = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

Average Speed = (D × U) ÷ B = (B² − S²) ÷ B when traveling equal distances upstream and downstream.</p

questions.question: A man can row a distance of 900 metres against the stream in 12 minutes and returns to the starting point in 9 minutes. What is the speed (in km/h) of the man in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Upstream Speed = 900 m ÷ 12 min = 75 m/min

Downstream Speed = 900 m ÷ 9 min = 100 m/min

Speed in still water = (100 + 75) ÷ 2 = 87.5 m/min

To km/h: 87.5 × (60 ÷ 1000) = 5.25 km/h

5.25 km/h = 5 ¹/₄ km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 5 1/4 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Distance = 900 m, Upstream time = 12 min, Downstream time = 9 min.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Speed in still water = (Downstream speed + Upstream speed) ÷ 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/44bb61347b5b4c9972b900ca2a2f4f3f1256bcc36c682e9778fdaa91a26c4051.png] 

⇒ Upstream speed = 0.9 ÷ (12/60) = 0.9 × 5 = 4.5 km/h

⇒ Downstream speed = 0.9 ÷ (9/60) = 0.9 × (60/9) = 6 km/h

⇒ Speed in still water = (6 + 4.5) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed = 10.5 ÷ 2 = 5.25 km/h

⇒ 5.25 = 5 ²⁵/₁₀₀ = 5 ¹/₄ km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 5 1/4 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speed

If the boat speed is u and stream speed is v, Downstream speed = u + v and Upstream speed = u − v.

Speed of Stream

Speed of current/stream (v) = (Downstream speed − Upstream speed) ÷ 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert m/min to km/h, multiply the value by 60 and divide by 1000 (or multiply by 0.06).</p

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the current is 6 km/h. In how much time (in hours) will the boat travel a distance of 90 km upstream and the same distance downstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream Speed (v + u) = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h

Upstream Speed (v − u) = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h

Total Time = (Distance ÷ Downstream Speed) + (Distance ÷ Upstream Speed)

Total Time = (90 ÷ 24) + (90 ÷ 12) = 3.75 + 7.5 = 11.25 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 11¼ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat (B) = 18 km/h

Speed of current (C) = 6 km/h

Distance (D) = 90 km

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/98561175f410925c994600bae653a514e1225f020214712d4bc73fc7a34f193e.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat + Speed of current

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of current

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h

⇒ Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h

⇒ Time for downstream trip = 90 ÷ 24 = 3.75 hours

⇒ Time for upstream trip = 90 ÷ 12 = 7.5 hours

⇒ Total time = 3.75 + 7.5 = 11.25 hours

⇒ 11.25 hours = 11 + 0.25 = 11 + (1/4) = 11¼ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 11¼ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed in Still Water

If downstream speed (D) and upstream speed (U) are known, Speed of boat = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Current

If downstream speed (D) and upstream speed (U) are known, Speed of current = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

Average Speed = (Downstream Speed × Upstream Speed) ÷ Still Water Speed = (D × U) ÷ B.</p

questions.question: If a boat goes upstream at a speed of 21 km/h and comes back the same distance at 28 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/hr) for the total journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance covered is the same for two different speeds, use the harmonic mean formula.

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Average Speed = (2 × 21 × 28) ÷ (21 + 28)

Average Speed = 1176 ÷ 49 = 24 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Upstream Speed (u) = 21 km/h, Downstream Speed (v) = 28 km/h.

Formula Used: Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e512f9c7c0eda0ae75d901ac50800b7ca64ad7ce9791ac041412ba5da353a8d.png] 

⇒ Let the distance for one way be the LCM of 21 and 28, which is 84 km.

⇒ Total Distance = 84 + 84 = 168 km

⇒ Time taken (Upstream) = Distance ÷ Speed = 84 ÷ 21 = 4 hours

⇒ Time taken (Downstream) = Distance ÷ Speed = 84 ÷ 28 = 3 hours

⇒ Total Time = 4 + 3 = 7 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 168 ÷ 7 = 24 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Average Speed Formula

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. This applies regardless of whether distances or times are equal.

Boat Speed in Still Water

Boat Speed (x) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2. In this case, x = (28 + 21) ÷ 2 = 24.5 km/h.

Speed of Stream

Stream Speed (y) = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2. In this case, y = (28 − 21) ÷ 2 = 3.5 km/h.

Average Speed for Equal Time

If time taken for both speeds is equal, Average Speed = (S₁ + S₂) ÷ 2 (Arithmetic Mean).</p

questions.question: If a boat goes upstream at a speed of 18 km/hr and comes back the same distance at 30 km/hr. What is the average speed (in km/hr) for the total journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance covered is the same for two different speeds, use the Harmonic Mean formula.

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Average Speed = (2 × 18 × 30) ÷ (18 + 30)

Average Speed = 1080 ÷ 48 = 22.5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 22.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Upstream Speed (U) = 18 km/hr

Downstream Speed (D) = 30 km/hr

Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/064c57f5713012aa00678fe5d5f170305e5596b21752ebd283fb255fd2c1186b.png] 

⇒ Let the distance for one side be the LCM of speeds (18, 30) = 90 km.

⇒ Time taken for Upstream (T₁) = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 hours

⇒ Time taken for Downstream (T₂) = Distance ÷ Downstream Speed = 90 ÷ 30 = 3 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 90 + 90 = 180 km

⇒ Total Time = 5 + 3 = 8 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 180 ÷ 8

⇒ Average Speed = 22.5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 22.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

It is calculated as the average of the downstream and upstream speeds: B = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream

It is calculated as half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: S = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Downstream and Upstream Relation

Downstream Speed = Speed of Boat + Speed of Current | Upstream Speed = Speed of Boat − Speed of Current.

Average Speed (General Case)

If distances d₁, d₂ are different, Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂) ÷ (t₁ + t₂).</p

questions.question: A boat can travel 104 km downstream in 8 hours. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, then find in what time will it be able to cover 13 km upstream?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed = 104 ÷ 8 = 13 km/h.

Upstream speed = Downstream speed − (2 × Speed of stream)

Upstream speed = 13 − (2 × 2) = 9 km/h.

Time for 13 km upstream = 13 ÷ 9 = 1 4/9 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 4/9 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Downstream distance = 104 km

Downstream time = 8 hours

Speed of stream (v) = 2 km/h

Upstream distance = 13 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Downstream speed (D) = u + v

Upstream speed (U) = u − v

Where u = speed of boat in still water and v = speed of stream.

 
• 
 

 Downstream: 104 km / 8 hrs = 13 km/h
 
• 
 

 Upstream: Distance = 13 km
 Result: Time = 13 ÷ 9 = 1 4/9 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream speed (D) = 104 ÷ 8 = 13 km/h

⇒ u + v = 13

⇒ u + 2 = 13

⇒ u = 13 − 2 = 11 km/h

⇒ Upstream speed (U) = u − v = 11 − 2 = 9 km/h

⇒ Time taken = Distance ÷ Upstream speed

⇒ Time taken = 13 ÷ 9 = 1 4/9 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 1 4/9 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speed

Downstream speed (D) = Speed of boat in still water (u) + Speed of stream (v). Upstream speed (U) = u − v.

Speed of Boat in Still Water

The speed of the boat in still water can be calculated as u = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream

The speed of the current or stream can be calculated as v = (D − U) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: If a boat goes upstream at a speed of 24 km/hr and comes back the same distance at 40 km/hr. What is the average speed (in km/hr) for the total journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance traveled is the same for both parts of the journey, use the harmonic mean formula.

Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y)

Where x = 24 km/hr and y = 40 km/hr.

Average Speed = (2 × 24 × 40) ÷ (24 + 40) = 1920 ÷ 64 = 30 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Upstream Speed (u) = 24 km/hr

Downstream Speed (v) = 40 km/hr

Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70e63365e330d85a0d9ecd89dbdf2618bc8bc4bf2b3c67b78ffd683dd9a2a4d1.png] 

⇒ Let the distance between the two points be the LCM of 24 and 40.

⇒ LCM(24, 40) = 120 km.

⇒ Time taken while going upstream (t₁) = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 hours.

⇒ Time taken while coming back downstream (t₂) = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 hours.

⇒ Total Distance = 120 + 120 = 240 km.

⇒ Total Time = 5 + 3 = 8 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 240 ÷ 8 = 30 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

It is the average of downstream and upstream speeds: Speedbₒₐₜ = (Downstream + Upstream) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream (Current)

It is half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: Speedₛₜᵣₑₐₘ = (Downstream − Upstream) ÷ 2.

General Average Speed

For unequal distances, Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂ + ... + dₙ) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + ... + tₙ).</p

questions.question: Find the time taken by a boat to travel 80 km with the current, if the speed of the boat in still water is 14 km/h and the speed of the current is 6 km/h.
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of a boat in still water = 14 km/h

Distance covered = 80 km 

Speed of the current = 6 km/h

Formulas used:

Speed downstream = Speed of boat + Speed of stream 

Time = Distance/Speed 

Calculation:

Downstream speed = 14 + 6 = 20 km/h

Let the time taken be = t 

80 km/(20) = t

⇒ 4 = t

⇒ t = 4 h

∴ The Time taken by boat to travel 80 km downstream is 4 hours.
